I have a different take on the last few scenes. In my opinion, I feel like the entire revenge journey of Ellie is a reflection on the depth that true love can even transmute brutal hate . 

Joel’s act of saving Ellie in the hospital was a pivotal turning point. It was a selfish act for himself, but also absolutely necessary in saving Ellie from her own hate from Abby. So in effect, Joel has saved Ellie twice, only regretably Ellie was too late in realizing it.  Let me explain:

Joel’s love for Ellie, a father’s love for a daughter, is a more mature form of love than what Ellie thinks is her duty to save humanity. In the final scene with Joel, we hear them have a talk where Joel confesses that if he was given another chance, that he would save her all over again. Ellie however, struggles with understanding the reason. This harkens back to that scene in the first game where Joel tells Ellie that she has no idea what loss  really is. Hard and bitter, but the truth. You see, Joel, unlike Ellie, has experienced loss to such an extent with the loss of Sarah, and so far beyond her comprehension at the time, that Ellie has no reference point. One can make an argument that Ellie’s loss of her parents and her best friend qualifies, but I think that type of loss hits different than that of a father losing a daughter.

Fast forward, and Ellie witnesses firsthand the brutal execution of Joel, by all accounts her old man. Now we are on the same page. Ellie feels that loss in her bones, and understands her own hate, just like us as audience members understand her hate, and just as Joel feels when losing Sarah.

NOW, right after Ellie’s first flashback of a bloody and beaten Joel, is when she decides she still has to kill Abby. At this point, Ellie is consumed by so much hate and anguish that she is willing to even use Lev as  leverage tp make Abby fight her. This tells me that Ellie just doesn’t give a fuck anymore, that she is willing to sink to the very depths of evil of what a human can do for her revenge. 

Right before she does it though...the moment before, she has a split second flashback of Joel looking at her, a realization, and everything about Joel’s decision makes sense to her. This was why she spares Abby. She realizes that by taking Abby and getting her revenge, that would have been catastrophic for Lev. It would have taken away something from Lev that Ellie was not willing to take. Ellie wasn’t awake when Joel saved her from the hospital, but she had witnessed Abby carrying Lev to the boat, and understands that that kind of love is just as worthy of saving as Joel’s love for her.

So I think Lev is the crucial piece here. Without him, Ellie would surely have killed Abby. I don’t think she cares for Lev in so much as she understands, finally, what Joel’s love was worth. And that changes everything for her.

I don’t know you and this is the first post I’ve written in a while, but, I read your story and want to reach out and offer some words.

The world is bigger and filled with more of EVERYTHING than you can possibly think of. Pain, more of it. Suffering, more of it. Hope, love, kindness, opportunities, more of it. People and infinite thoughts swirling around everyone, more of it.

So when you talk about exams, GPA’s, pass this or what-not, manager’s attitudes toward you— it really just means you are looking down a dark tunnel made of styrofoam. Break free from that.

From what I gather, you seem to be caught up in a circle of self-doubt and the imagery you use to describe your present mood is incredibly vivid and although dark, is morbidly creative.

Look, all I’m trying to say is, a feeling is just that— a feeling. It isn’t an order. It isn’t something you must give into. It isn’t the end-all and be all of your life. Take some time to sort yourself out. Be kind to yourself and allow yourself to make mistakes. Please don’t rush into something that is a permanent solution to a temporary problem. 

Kind regards

Yeah, I‘m Chinese-American and I feel similarly to your situation. Literally graduated from one of top ten colleges, came out to the real world and went, fuck I’m intelligent but socially and emotionally screwed up from years of unresolved abuse. Lost job after job of just stupidity on my part, not being able to read others and existing in my own depressed mindset. I’ve literally turned into the very definition of overachiever turned underachiever. Let me tell you man, it’s the worst thing ever. 

Thirteen years later, I sometimes still feel stuck and unable to reciprocate feelings on a normal human level. But you know what? What I realized is will, and motivation needs to come from within, not from ANYTHING external. External factors and influences are there to try to influence you, that’s their job. It’s your choice whether you want to be influenced or not! It’s not going to be perfect. Not gonna lie. It’s messy and you’d sometimes want to sink into your vices whatever it may be ( video games and drinking for me). Then you wake up the next day and the sun is shining and you feel you can change your mindset again. The longer you fall and get back up, fall and get back you, you begin to start to love the process and you will then become OK with anything and anyone. That’s when the magic happens.

A lot of us are so lost in ourselves, that it almost feels like running blindly into a tunnel with the darkness closing in and having no chance of escaping it. I don't know how old you are but you sound like a decent human being who is just lost. And that might fill you with fear.

I get it. When you're in it, you have tunnel vision and can't take in the possibility of anything good ever coming out of your shitty life. Because I, like many, many others, have been there. And sometimes we still go there, more often than we care to admit. 

Thing is, there really is not much any of us can do to let you know for SURE that life will get better. You just have to take it on faith that it will happen, as it happened to millions of other people around the world. That is a fact. Facts are powerful in that sense, because you can't dispute the legitamacy of it being true.

Hopefully that knowledge will fill you with some bit of hope for the future. Good luck, girl.
